items.pronunciation_notes: Short 'a' as in 'cut', never as in 'cat'. Every consonant carries this vowel automatically, and word-finally it drops: कमल is kamal, not kamala.
items.gloss_en: short vowel a — the inherent vowel

learn.title_en: अ — the vowel that is already there
learn.explanation_en: अ is a short 'a', the vowel in English 'cut', not the one in 'cat'. It is the only vowel with no matra symbol, because every consonant is assumed to carry it already — क on its own reads 'ka'. English speakers make two mistakes with it: they stretch it into a long 'aa', and they pronounce the final one that Hindi speakers drop.

examples.note: Opens with the short अ; the long vowel comes in the second syllable.
क and म each carry an unwritten अ, but the final one is not pronounced.
Two letters, one syllable — the अ inside ब drops away.

common_error.why_en: The first vowel is the short अ, not the long आ. Vowel length is part of the word in Hindi, not a matter of emphasis.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which vowel does this word start with?
practice.question: अनार
practice.explanation_en: The word opens with the short vowel अ. The long आ appears later, in the second syllable.

game.question_en: Three of these words begin with the short अ sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: आम opens with the long vowel आ, held about twice as long. The other three open with short अ.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long आ, roughly twice the length of अ. As a matra it is the vertical stroke written after the consonant: क plus ा gives का.

learn.title_en: आ — the long partner of अ
learn.explanation_en: आ uses the same mouth position as अ but is held about twice as long, like the a in 'father'. Written after a consonant it becomes the matra ा. Length carries meaning here, so shortening आ produces a different word — कम and काम are not variants of one another.

examples.note: Written in full because nothing comes before it.
The same vowel, now written as the matra ा attached to क.
Both syllables are long; the final ा is written and pronounced.

common_error.why_en: Dropping the matra changes the word: कम means 'less', काम means 'work'.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which vowel do you hear in the first syllable?
practice.question: काम
practice.explanation_en: The vertical stroke after क makes the vowel long — kaam, not kam.

game.question_en: Three of these words contain the long आ sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: कम carries no matra, so its vowel is the short अ. The other three all have ा.

items.pronunciation_notes: Short i as in 'sit'. Its matra ि is written to the LEFT of the consonant but pronounced after it: कि reads 'ki'.

learn.title_en: इ — and the matra that jumps left
learn.explanation_en: इ is a short i, as in English 'sit'. Its matra is ि, and it is the one matra written to the left of its consonant even though it is spoken after it — कि is read 'ki', never 'ik'. Learners sounding words out letter by letter get this backwards for the first week or so; expect it and read the pair as a unit.

examples.note: Opens with the full letter इ because nothing precedes it.
The matra sits to the left of क but is pronounced after it.
One syllable: द with the ि matra, then न with its vowel dropped.

common_error.why_en: The first vowel is the short इ. Using the long ी matra gives a spelling that does not exist.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which vowel do you hear in the first syllable?
practice.question: किताब
practice.explanation_en: The matra on क is the short one — kitaab. The long ी would give 'kii', which is not how the word is said.

game.question_en: Three of these words have the short इ sound in the first syllable. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: दीवार begins with the long ई sound. The other three carry the short इ.

summary.recap_en: This level introduced अ, आ and इ, and the idea that every consonant already carries an अ unless a matra replaces it. It also showed the first matra that is written on the wrong side of its consonant.
summary.next_up_en: Next: ई, उ and ऊ, where vowel length starts separating one word from another.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long ee as in 'seen'. The matra ी is written after the consonant — the opposite side from its short partner ि.

learn.title_en: ई — length that changes the word
learn.explanation_en: ई is the long partner of इ, like the ee in 'seen'. Its matra ी goes on the right of the consonant, which is the mirror image of ि. Because Hindi treats vowel length as meaningful, दिन and दीन are two different words — a vowel held too long is not an accent, it is a different word.

examples.note: The full letter, used at the start of a word.
The matra follows न and is held long.
Long ई in the first syllable, long आ in the second.

common_error.why_en: नीला needs the long ी. The short ि gives a syllable a Hindi speaker will not read as this word.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which matra is in the first syllable?
practice.question: नीला
practice.explanation_en: The stroke sits after न and is held long — niilaa. The short ि would be written before न.

game.question_en: Three of these words have a long ई sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: दिन has the short इ matra. The other three all carry the long ई.

items.pronunciation_notes: Short u as in 'put', never the 'yoo' of English 'use'. The matra ु hooks under the consonant. In उल्लू the doubled ल is held slightly longer.

learn.explanation_en: उ is a short, rounded u, the vowel in English 'put'. Its matra ु hooks under the consonant. English speakers often import the 'yoo' sound from words like 'use' or 'unit'; Hindi never does that, and the vowel is always short unless the deeper double hook is written.

examples.note: Short उ first, long ऊ at the end — the two lengths side by side in one word.
The matra hangs below ब and stays short.
Short उ in the first syllable; the final vowel is not written at all.

common_error.why_en: बुरा takes the short hook. The long ू stretches the syllable and sounds to a listener like a different word.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which vowel do you hear in the first syllable?
practice.question: बुरा
practice.explanation_en: The single hook under ब is the short उ — buraa, said briskly.

game.question_en: Three of these words begin with the short उ sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: ऊपर opens with the long ऊ. The other three open with the short उ.

items.pronunciation_notes: Long oo as in 'food'. Its matra ू is a deeper double hook under the consonant, easy to confuse with the short ु in handwriting.

learn.explanation_en: ऊ is the long partner of उ, like the oo in 'food'. Under a consonant it is written ू, a deeper hook than the short ु. The difference is not decorative: चुना means 'chose' and चूना means 'lime'. In handwriting the two hooks look similar, so read the whole word before deciding.

examples.note: The full letter at the start of a word.
The long hook under फ — hold the vowel clearly.
A long vowel in one of the most frequent words you will ever say.

common_error.why_en: The vowel in दूध is long. Shortening it is the single most common English-speaker slip in this word.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which matra is under the first consonant?
practice.question: दूध
practice.explanation_en: The deeper double hook under द is the long ऊ — duudh.

game.question_en: Three of these words have the long ऊ sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: सुबह has the short hook ु. The other three all carry the long ऊ.

summary.recap_en: This level added ई, उ and ऊ, and established that vowel length is not a matter of accent — it separates one word from another.
summary.next_up_en: Next: ए, ऐ and ओ, whose matras sit above the line and which English speakers tend to add a glide to.

items.pronunciation_notes: A steady 'ay' with no glide at the end — not the English 'day', which slides into a y sound.

learn.title_en: ए — a steady vowel, no glide
learn.explanation_en: ए is close to the vowel in English 'bed' but longer and, crucially, flat. English speakers slide 'ay' into a y at the end; Hindi holds the vowel level from start to finish. Its matra े is a single small stroke above the consonant. Adding the glide is the fastest way to sound foreign in an otherwise correct sentence.

examples.note: Two letters, one syllable — the final vowel of क drops.
The stroke sits above म and the vowel stays flat.
Hold the vowel level; do not let it drift towards a y.

common_error.why_en: ऐ is a separate, more open vowel. Writing two strokes where one belongs gives a form nobody will read as 'my'.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which vowel do you hear in the first syllable?
practice.question: मेरा
practice.explanation_en: The single stroke above म gives the flat ए. ऐ would open the mouth noticeably wider.

game.question_en: Three of these words have the ए sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: पैसा carries the wider ऐ. The other three have the flat, narrower ए.

items.pronunciation_notes: In standard Hindi this is a single open vowel close to the a in 'cat' — not the 'eye' diphthong its usual transliteration suggests.

learn.explanation_en: ऐ is transliterated 'ai', which misleads English speakers into saying 'eye'. In standard spoken Hindi it is one open vowel, close to the a in 'cat'. Its matra ै is a double stroke above the consonant — one stroke more than ए. The word है, the commonest word in the language, is said 'heh', not 'high'.

examples.note: Open ऐ in the first syllable — closer to 'pessa' than to 'pie-sa'.
You will say this thousands of times. Get the vowel flat and open.
Open ऐ then flat ए — neither vowel glides.

common_error.why_en: पैसा needs the wider ऐ. The single stroke gives the narrower ए and a different-sounding word.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which matra is written above the consonant?
practice.question: है
practice.explanation_en: Two strokes above ह mark ऐ, the open vowel heard in hai.

game.question_en: Three of these words have the ऐ sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: देश has the flat ए. The other three carry the more open ऐ.

items.pronunciation_notes: A pure long o with no glide — English 'go' ends in a small w sound, and Hindi does not.

learn.explanation_en: ओ is a long o held steady, like the vowel in Scottish 'boat'. English speakers finish the sound with a small w, which marks an accent immediately even when the grammar is perfect. Its matra ो combines the ा stroke with a mark above the line.

examples.note: The full letter at the start of a word.
The vowel stays flat all the way through.
One short word, one steady vowel, no w at the end.

common_error.why_en: औ is a separate, more open vowel. दौ is not a word.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which vowel do you hear in the first syllable?
practice.question: सोना
practice.explanation_en: The matra gives a flat, steady o — sonaa, with no w sound at the end.

game.question_en: Three of these words have the ओ sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: पैसा has the open ऐ. The other three all carry the flat ओ.

summary.recap_en: This level covered ए, ऐ and ओ and the habit English speakers need to break: Hindi's mid vowels are held flat, without the y or w glide English adds automatically.
summary.next_up_en: Next: औ and ऋ finish the vowel set, and aspiration introduces the first contrast English marks without knowing it.

levels.title_en: The last vowels, and the puff of air

items.pronunciation_notes: A single open vowel closer to the aw of 'law' than to the 'ow' of 'cow'.

learn.explanation_en: औ stands to ओ exactly as ऐ stands to ए: same region of the mouth, more open. Transliterated 'au', it tempts English speakers into the 'ow' of 'cow', but standard Hindi keeps it a single vowel nearer the aw of 'law'. Its matra ौ carries two strokes where ो carries one.

examples.note: One of the most frequent words in the language — worth getting right on day one.
Open औ, then a plain न.
Two letters, one open vowel, no glide.

common_error.why_en: कौन needs the open औ. The single-stroke matra gives the narrower ओ.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which vowel do you hear?
practice.question: कौन
practice.explanation_en: Two strokes above क mark औ, the open vowel heard in kaun.

game.question_en: Three of these words have the औ sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: दो has the flat ओ. The other three carry the more open औ.

items.pronunciation_notes: Historically a vocalic r; in modern Hindi it is simply pronounced 'ri'. कृपया is kripayaa, and the final vowel of अमृत drops.

learn.title_en: ऋ — written as a vowel, said as 'ri'
learn.explanation_en: ऋ is counted as a vowel and was once a vocalic r, but modern Hindi speakers simply say 'ri'. You will meet it almost only in words borrowed from Sanskrit. Its matra ृ hooks under the consonant. Do not chase an exotic sound — say कृपया as 'kripayaa' and you are correct; the only real difficulty is spelling, since the sound gives no clue that a vowel rather than र is written.

examples.note: The full letter, used at the start of a word.
The matra sits under क and the syllable is read 'kri'.
Read 'mri' in the middle, and the final vowel is not pronounced.

common_error.why_en: The sound really is 'ri', but the spelling uses the vowel ऋ, not र with a matra.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which sign does this word use?
practice.question: कृपया
practice.explanation_en: The hook under क is ऋ, read 'ri' — kripayaa, not kupayaa or kipayaa.

game.question_en: Three of these words are spelt with ऋ. Which one is not?
game.explanation_en: रात is written with the consonant र plus a matra. The other three use the vowel ऋ.

items.pronunciation_notes: ख is क plus a puff of breath. The English k in 'kite' is already aspirated, so English speakers produce ख when they intend क — the unaspirated one is the harder sound for them.

learn.title_en: Aspiration: the puff that changes the word
learn.explanation_en: Hindi treats a puff of breath as part of the letter itself. क is said with no breath at all, ख with a clear puff; प has no puff, फ has one. English uses both sounds unconsciously — the k in 'kite' is aspirated, the k in 'skate' is not — so English speakers default to the puffed version and say खोना when they mean कोना. Hold a hand in front of your mouth: क and प should not move it.

examples.note: No breath on the first sound — a paper held in front of your mouth stays still.
Same word shape, one puff of air, completely different meaning.
The same contrast in the p-family. फ is p with breath, not the English f.

common_error.why_en: Meaning 'corner' but adding English's automatic puff of breath turns the noun into the verb 'to lose'.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which consonant starts this word?
practice.question: फल
practice.explanation_en: There is a clear puff of breath after the p, so it is फ — phal, 'fruit'. Without the puff it would be पल, 'a moment'.

game.question_en: Three of these words begin with an unaspirated consonant — no puff of air. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: खोना begins with ख, which carries the puff. The others begin with क or प, said with no breath at all.

summary.recap_en: This level finished the vowel set with औ and ऋ, and introduced the first contrast English marks without noticing: aspiration, where a puff of breath is part of the letter and changes the word.
summary.next_up_en: Next: retroflex against dental, the two nasal marks, and the sound of व — the three contrasts English gives you no habits at all for.

levels.title_en: Three contrasts English does not mark

items.pronunciation_notes: Retroflex ट and ड curl the tongue tip back to the roof of the mouth; dental त and द press the tongue flat against the back of the upper teeth. The English t and d sit between the two and are heard by Hindi speakers as retroflex.

learn.title_en: Retroflex and dental: two t's, two d's
learn.explanation_en: Hindi splits what English hears as one t into two letters. For ट the tongue tip curls back and taps the roof of the mouth; for त it presses flat against the back of the upper teeth. The English t lands between them and Hindi ears file it as retroflex, so an English speaker asking for दाल usually produces डाल instead. The same split runs through ड and द, and through ण and न.

examples.note: Dental — tongue against the teeth. This is the everyday food word.
Retroflex — tongue curled back. Order this at dinner and you have asked for a tree branch.
Both t sounds here are retroflex, despite what the English spelling suggests.

common_error.why_en: English speakers curl the tongue back by default, which turns the word for lentils into the word for a branch.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which consonant starts this word?
practice.question: दाल
practice.explanation_en: The tongue touches the back of the upper teeth and the sound is voiced, so it is the dental द — daal, 'lentils'.

game.question_en: Three of these words begin with a retroflex sound. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: दाल begins with the dental द. The other three start with the tongue curled back to the roof of the mouth.

items.pronunciation_notes: ं closes the syllable with a real nasal consonant matching whatever follows; ँ nasalises the vowel itself and adds no consonant. हंस is hans, हँस is hãs.

learn.title_en: Two dots that are not interchangeable
learn.explanation_en: The plain dot ं closes a syllable with a real nasal consonant, chosen to match the sound that follows: हिंदी is 'hindii', अंडा is 'aṇḍaa'. The moon-dot ँ adds no consonant at all — it just sends the vowel through the nose. हंस is a swan; हँस is the command 'laugh'. Learners who treat the two marks as one mark misspell and mishear both words.

examples.note: The dot closes the syllable with an n before the s.
The vowel hums through the nose and no n is pronounced.
Here the plain dot is read as n because द follows it.

common_error.why_en: The verb 'to laugh' takes the moon-dot. The plain dot points at the noun for a swan instead.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which mark does this word need?
practice.question: हँस
practice.explanation_en: Nothing is pronounced after the vowel — the vowel itself hums — so this is the moon-dot ँ.

game.question_en: In three of these words the nasal mark is pronounced as a full consonant. In which one is only the vowel nasalised?
game.explanation_en: हँसना carries the moon-dot, so no n is heard. The other three use the plain dot, which closes the syllable with n or ṇ.

items.pronunciation_notes: For व the lower lip approaches the upper teeth without pressing — lighter than an English v, firmer than a w. Its exact colour varies by word and speaker and both are accepted; ब, by contrast, closes the lips completely.
items.gloss_en: the sound व — between English v and w — against ब

example_word.english: a blow / a time, an occasion

learn.explanation_en: English has two separate sounds, v and w, and swapping them changes words: 'vet' and 'wet'. Hindi has one sound sitting between them — the lower lip comes close to the upper teeth but does not press. That means you cannot get it wrong by choosing between v and w; Hindi speakers hear no difference. What does go wrong is pressing too hard, because a firm English v drifts towards ब, which is a different letter and a different word.

examples.note: Written this way, but usually said 'vo' in everyday speech.
Light contact between lip and teeth — the lips never meet.
Full lip closure. Same word shape, different letter, different meaning.

common_error.why_en: Closing the lips fully turns व into ब. वापस, 'back', keeps the lips apart.

practice.prompt_en: Listen. Which consonant starts this word?
practice.question: वापस
practice.explanation_en: The lips never close — the lower lip only approaches the teeth — so this is व, not ब.

game.question_en: Three of these words begin with व. Which one does not?
game.explanation_en: बार closes the lips completely for ब. The other three use the lighter व, with the lips apart.

summary.recap_en: This level covered the three contrasts English gives no habits for: retroflex against dental, the plain dot against the moon-dot, and the single Hindi sound व that sits between English v and w.
summary.next_up_en: Module 2 begins the consonants proper, family by family, starting with the क-family and the aspiration drill introduced here.
